name: Sanjaya Belatthiputta
dates_notes: Placed broadly among the early Śramaṇa teachers known from Buddhist narrative and doxographical sources; no independent chronology or corpus survives.
evidence_basis: Buddhist reports, especially the account of the six contemporary teachers, with parallel recensional evidence.
core_thesis: Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta is reported in Buddhist sources as refusing to settle contested metaphysical questions through a style of non-committal answer later called *amarāvikkhepa*. The reports make him an important early counterpoint to systems that offer determinate claims about the self, cosmic order, moral causation, or post-mortem survival. They do not preserve a self-authored sceptical theory, so this entry records a reconstructed position rather than a securely bounded school or a biography with recoverable doctrine beyond the reported suspension of judgment.
